executionRestrictions.sourceVersusPolicy: On-chain Multicall itself is selector-agnostic and would allow empty/nested batches. executionRestrictions.native: The source performs sequential address(this).delegatecall(data[i]); actual EVM msg.sender and msg.value are preserved, not replaced with the router. Router balance is shared across operations; use zero native value unless intentionally required.
executionRestrictions.grantsAndPauses: Catalog admission is not a grant. Custom mode independently requires the exact root ID and every actually used child ID; unused listed children need no grant. All mode retains broad active-capability semantics and all global/chain/contract/root/child pauses. executionRestrictions.finalAcceptance: Unchanged reviewed manifest/ABI/scope hashes, request commitment, exact plan recomputation/equality, live API-key mode/grants/revocation/expiry/freeze/ownership and independent transaction/send policies at final acceptance under existing pause/key locks. financialRiskNotes: Router native/ERC20 custody is public shared surplus, not caller-attributed escrow. Sweep/unwrap/refund can transfer whole balances; recipients and fee recipients remain caller-selected where exposed. Stranded balances can be recovered by other callers. A batch does not insert settlement/refund or prove that no balance remains.

Existing balance, ERC20 allowances and fixed-dependency approvals must already suffice. Router02 structured mint/increaseLiquidity use only the source-constructed position-manager calls and any preexisting router-to-manager allowances; no approve/permit capability or opaque callPositionManager(bytes) is admitted.

## Universal Router

The `UniversalRouter` contract is the current preferred entrypoint for ERC20 and NFT swaps, replacing, among other contracts, `SwapRouter02`. An up-to-date list of [deploy addresses by chain is hosted on GitHub](https://github.com/Uniswap/universal-router/tree/main/deploy-addresses).

## Uniswap Pool Deployments

Every Uniswap pool is a unique instance of the `UniswapV3Pool` contract and is deployed at its own unique address. The contract source code of the pool will be auto-verified on etherscan. For example, here is the [ETH/USDC 0.3% pool](https://etherscan.io/address/0x8ad599c3a0ff1de082011efddc58f1908eb6e6d8) on Ethereum mainnet.

You can look up the address of an existing pool on [Uniswap Info](https://info.uniswap.org/#/) or by calling the `getPool` function on the `UniswapV3Factory` contract.

```solidity
getPool("0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48", "0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2", 3000)
```

## Wrapped Native Token Addresses

The Uniswap Protocol supports trading of ERC20 tokens. In order to swap a native asset like ETH (or MATIC on Polygon), the Uniswap protocol wraps these assets in an ERC20 wrapped native token contract. The protocol uses the following WETH9 addresses on Ethereum and WMATIC addresses on Polygon.
